parts.label: (a)
parts.stem:
An unlabelled bottle contains a straight-chain halogenoalkane, $\mathbf{Q}$. The molecular formula of $\mathbf{Q}$ is $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{11}\mathbf{X}$, where $\mathbf{X}$ is a halogen; bromine, chlorine or iodine.

A test is carried out to identify the halogen present in $\mathbf{Q}$.
A sample of $\mathbf{Q}$ is added to $\text{NaOH(aq)}$ and warmed. Dilute nitric acid is then added followed by a few drops of aqueous silver nitrate. A cream precipitate is observed.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Write an ionic equation to describe the formation of the cream precipitate. Include state symbols.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: Describe a further test which would confirm the identity of $\mathbf{X}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: The reaction of $\mathbf{Q}$ with $\text{NaOH(aq)}$ tends to proceed via an $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ mechanism.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Suggest the structural formula of the straight-chain halogenoalkane $\mathbf{Q}$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why the reaction tends to proceed via an $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ mechanism rather than an $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ mechanism.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem:
Two different halogenoalkanes, $\mathbf{P}$ and $\mathbf{R}$, both with the molecular formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{Cl}$, are separately dissolved in ethanol and heated under reflux with sodium hydroxide.

The major organic product of each of these reactions is methylpropene.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Name the type of reaction occurring.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Write an equation, using molecular formulae, to represent the reaction occurring.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Draw the skeletal formula of methylpropene.
